Games Action Games Grand Theft Auto GTA 6 It's not just GTA 6 - Take-Two boss argues "we have the best collection" of IP in the business thanks to Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and more News By Catherine Lewis Published 5 November 2026 Grand Theft Auto is far from the company's only big hitter When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here's how it works . (Image credit: Rockstar) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter With GTA 6 right around the corner, Rockstar Games and its owner Take-Two Interactive will be getting ready to enjoy the fruits of their labor with a massive launch, especially if current pre-order estimates are anything to go by. But GTA isn't Take-Two's only breadwinner - CEO Strauss Zelnick reckons that "we have the best collection" of IP in the games business. Speaking in a new interview with the Wall Street Journal (below), Zelnick defends the strength of Take-Two's full library, which may be boosted by GTA, but by no means relies on it entirely. "We have 15 franchises that have each sold at least 5 million units in an individual release," he begins. "I think we have the best collection of owned intellectual property in the video game business, and I think that's reflected in our top line, our bottom line, and our market cap." Latest Videos From GamesRadar+ Watch full video here: The CEO Behind Grand Theft Auto VI at WSJ Tech | WSJ - YouTube Watch On He continues: "In addition to Grand Theft Auto, we have Red Dead Redemption, a massive title. It sold over 65 million units in the most recent release. Red Dead Online, Grand Theft Auto Online, we have NBA 2K, which is the second-biggest sports title worldwide - the biggest in North America." In a quickfire round, Zelnick also lists the likes of Borderlands, BioShock, WWE 2K, and Civilization, as well as mobile hits such as Words with Friends and Empires & Puzzles. You may like As GTA 6 hype builds as the industry buckles, Take-Two boss says "I don't love winning by attrition" With GTA 6 about to launch, Take-Two boss unloads on investor criticizing "years of delays" With GTA 6 delays, Take-Two CEO suggests Rockstar didn't want a Cyberpunk 2077 situation Depending on your personal preferences and biases, you may or may not agree with Zelnick that Take-Two truly has the best bank of IP - others like Nintendo could certainly give the company a run for its money with the likes of Mario, Zelda, and Smash Bros., not to mention its partial ownership of Pokemon. But there's definitely no denying its strength - even with the current highest-rated game of the year , The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , out today, it's hard to think of November as anything other than Rockstar's month. With GTA 6 delays, Take-Two CEO suggests Rockstar didn't want a Cyberpunk 2077 situation: "They had to pull the title after shipping."
